title: Alexandr Wang on building Scale AI: data as AI infrastructure and picking uncrowded ideas
summary: Wang explains how Scale became the data infrastructure layer for AI by focusing on a base primitive (data) that must scale as the industry scales. He gives founder advice: start before a trend is cool, avoid crowded categories, don't build ahead of the technology, and ignore small-TAM objections. He also shares his outlook on multimodality, proprietary data and enterprise AI.

principles.text: Build infrastructure around base primitives that can't be bypassed and must scale exponentially with the industry.
principles.quote: you can't build AI without data fundamentally and then it's something that um has to scale exponentially as the entire field develops

principles.text: Start in an area before it gets cool, so you have a head start when the opportunity arrives.
principles.quote: the thing that allows you to actually win is that by the time the thing becomes cool or interesting you've had this like head running Head Start

principles.text: Avoid crowded categories; pick unpopular areas where AI can still have a large impact.
principles.quote: I would pick I would pick areas uh which are not very popular

principles.text: Don't bet the company on technical limitations disappearing; stay within what the technology can do today.
principles.quote: don't try to start something that's too far ahead of where the capability of the technology is

principles.text: A blank-slate, naive approach lets you accomplish what incumbents stuck in ruts cannot.
principles.quote: approaching Industries with a totally blank slate and and no with Without A fine grain understanding of what makes things hard is actually part of what allows you to accomplish things

principles.text: Small TAM objections are normal for important companies in fast-growing markets; have conviction early.
principles.quote: the T was small of every important company when they were getting started basically
